column1: # The 324 function words of English: determiners, prepositions,
# conjunctions, pronouns, auxiliaries and modals, particles, numerals and
# common interjections. Wiktionary's dump for this project carries only noun,
# verb, adjective and adverb, so none of these words can come out of a built
# lexicon and every one of them would otherwise be reported no_analysis. They
# are the most frequent words in any English text, so that is the single
# largest hole a built lexicon leaves.
# POS is FUNCTION, which no inflectional or derivational rule matches, so each
# of these stems analyzes as itself and nothing else: "the" is one piece with
# gate lexicon_stem, and "thes" is not a plural. A word listed here that is
# also an open-class word elsewhere ("second", "light", "will", "can") keeps
# both readings, since each is its own lexeme.
# This file is NOT loaded by default. Pass it explicitly:
# Loading it by default would change the output of inputs that already had an
# analysis, which the segmentation contract fixes in place. See
# WEIGHT is 1.3 for every entry, the top of the frequency-derived scale in
# docs/LEXICON.md, because these are the most frequent words in English. It
# also settles the four words that are both a function word and a real
# inflected form: "being", "having", "doing" and "used" rank as single pieces
# here, with be + -ing and the rest still available under --nbest 2.
# Words are listed once each, under the category they belong to most
# centrally. Several belong to more than one ("but", "as", "since", "one",
# "over", "half"), and the morphology does not distinguish the categories in
# any case: see the note on PartOfSpeech::FUNCTION in LEXICON/lexeme.h.
